title: At the Theater
goal: Collect or choose tickets, find your seats, ask about the performance, and manage the intermission.

runs.text: The
box office
is where a venue sells or distributes tickets.
Will call
can mean collecting tickets already reserved or purchased. Ask
Where do I pick up my tickets?
if the signs or instructions are unclear.

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: I'm picking up two tickets under Casey Duncan.

turns.en: I'm picking up two tickets under Casey Duncan.

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Do you have your confirmation number?

turns.en: Do you have your confirmation number?

runs.text: Yes. It's WD2048.

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Thank you. Here are your tickets.

turns.en: Thank you. Here are your tickets.

blocks.caption: At the box office · Guest & Staff

runs.text: Confirmation number
or
order number
identifies the transaction; the venue may call it a
booking reference
. You can show the number or read it out.
I bought them online
explains how you purchased them; it does not tell staff your name or performance date.
Use these fictional performance facts in Practice:

rows.text: A Door in the Rain, tonight at 7:30 p.m.
Two orchestra seats, row B, seats 5 and 6; confirmation WD2048
Two balcony seats with a partly obstructed view
Two hours including one twenty-minute intermission
Begins at 8:30 p.m.; audience returns by 8:50 p.m.
Coat check available; no photography during this performance

runs.text: Are there any seats left for tonight?
checks availability.
Do those seats have a clear view?
checks a different detail. A
partly obstructed view
means something blocks part of what you can see. You may accept those seats or ask
What about tomorrow?

rows.text: Area where the performance takes place
Seats on the main floor, distinct from an orchestra's musicians
A line of seats / your individual place
The first row closest to the stage in that section
A small, partly separated group of seats
People watching / someone taking part in the show
Scenery and stage environment / an object used in the performance
Hanging material that can cover or frame the stage

runs.text: The venue's seating chart names its actual sections.
Orchestra
is useful for this fictional theater; not every room uses identical labels.
Theater
is the spelling used here; a venue's official name may use
Theatre
May I see your tickets?

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: Here you go. We're in row B.

turns.en: Here you go. We're in row B.

turns.speaker: Usher

runs.text: Seats five and six. This aisle, then the second row.

turns.en: Seats five and six. This aisle, then the second row.

runs.text: Thank you.
An
usher
helps people reach their seats. If someone is in yours, try
Excuse me. I think this is my seat. Could we check the tickets?
This lets you compare the details without assuming which person made the mistake.
Other useful questions are
How long is the show?
Is there an intermission?
Do you have a coat check?
, and
When is opening night?
Opening night marks the official opening of a production. Ask staff about a step-free route or other access need rather than infer one from a seat name.

study.title: Before the show and during the break

runs.text: The show is about to start
means it will start very soon. You may hear
Please silence your phones
or a request to switch them off. Respond to the instruction for that performance.
An
intermission
is a break between parts of the performance.
How long is the intermission?

turns.speaker: Usher

runs.text: Twenty minutes. Please be back by eight fifty.

turns.en: Twenty minutes. Please be back by eight fifty.

runs.text: Thanks. Where's the restroom?

turns.speaker: Usher

runs.text: In the lobby, to the right.

turns.en: In the lobby, to the right.

blocks.caption: Before the show and during the break · Guest & Usher

runs.text: Let's get a drink.

turns.speaker: You

runs.text: I'd rather stay here. I'll see you back at our seats.

turns.en: I'd rather stay here. I'll see you back at our seats.

turns.speaker: Companion

runs.text: Okay. I'll be back before eight fifty.

turns.en: Okay. I'll be back before eight fifty.

blocks.caption: Before the show and during the break · Companion & You

runs.text: If you arrive late,
Can we go in now?
asks about admission at that moment. Staff may say
Please wait here until we can seat you
. That is a response to follow, not a promise that every venue handles late entry the same way.
Speak both roles alone. Use the performance facts and supplied lobby direction.
Collect Casey Duncan's two tickets. Staff ask for the confirmation number; supply it and confirm the row and seats.

sample.text: Two tickets under Casey Duncan. The confirmation number is WD2048. We're in row B, seats five and six, right?

runs.text: You have no tickets. Ask about tonight and the view. Decline the partly obstructed seats and ask about tomorrow; staff offer the pair shown in the table.

sample.text: I'd prefer a clear view. Are there orchestra seats tomorrow?

runs.text: Show your ticket to an usher and ask where row B is. The usher gives the model's aisle and row instruction.

sample.text: We're in row B. Which aisle should we use?

runs.text: Someone is in seat 5. Ask to compare tickets. Their ticket is for seat 15, and they say
Oh, sorry. I read it wrong
. Respond briefly.

sample.text: I think this is my seat. Could we check our tickets? — Oh, sorry. — No problem.

runs.text: Ask the length of the intermission and return time. Your companion wants a drink; you prefer to stay. Arrange where to meet and when.

sample.text: When do we need to be back? — Eight fifty. — I'll stay here. See you at our seats before then.

runs.text: Hide the models. Re-create arrival and ticket collection with one changed detail. For late entry, staff say
Please wait here until we can seat you
; acknowledge that instruction.
Check:
Did the name, number and performance identify the tickets? Did your seat request account for the view? Did the meeting plan fit the return time?
